---
title: "Reconstructing disturbance interactions of wildfire and spruce beetle outbreaks across Alaska using SAR radar data and deep learning algorithms"
date: today
author:
  - name: Seamus Murphy
    orcid: 0000-0002-1792-0351
abstract: |
  Spruce beetle (*Dendroctonus rufipennis*) has killed spruce across
  Southcentral Alaska since about 2016, yet roughly ninety per cent of the
  mortality sits in stands of areal severity below 0.05, beneath the detection
  floor of Landsat change analysis, and the aerial survey understates this
  dispersed damage. Few studies have asked whether the temporal dimension of
  freely available satellite data reaches below that floor, and none has asked
  it of a spruce beetle outbreak with radar, which cloud does not stop. This
  study tests whether temporal deep learning on a monthly Sentinel-1 radar
  series lowers the floor, across 160 stand blocks over the Southcentral
  outbreak region (2017 to 2026) assigned wholly to eight spatial
  cross-validation folds. Terrain-corrected dual-polarisation
  backscatter from one satellite track, speckle-filtered across the length of
  the series at 10 m on the Equi7Grid, feeds a temporal convolutional network 
  and a Transformer encoder together with climate variables defined from the beetle's 
  biology, trained on dead-spruce crowns digitised from statewide sub-metre mosaics of
  2020 and 2023, whose comparison gives interval-censored onset labels. Skill
  is reported per severity stratum under block cross-validation against the
  published shortwave infrared floor and evaluated against an independent
  high-resolution severity product. [Detection skill in the 0.01 to 0.10
  stratum: pending.] [Detectability floor per method: pending.] [Onset-dating
  error and the effect of interval supervision: pending.] [Contribution of
  climate variables: pending.] [Correspondence of the reconstructed outbreak
  progression with the aerial survey record: pending.] The severity strata,
  metrics and decision rules were fixed by pre-registration before outcome
  data were analysed.

```{r}
frame_at_scale <- function(x, scale, width_in, height_in, crs = "EPSG:32605") {
  bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(x, crs))
  cx <- mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]); cy <- mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")])
  hw <- width_in  * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  hh <- height_in * 0.0254 * scale / 2
  sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - hw, ymin = cy - hh, xmax = cx + hw, ymax = cy + hh),
              crs = sf::st_crs(crs))
}
```

# Introduction

Outbreaks of the spruce beetle, *Dendroctonus rufipennis* (Kirby, 1837), Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae, have recurred in the spruce forests of Southcentral Alaska for centuries, with outbreak extent linked to summer temperature [@Berg_2006]. From 1990 to 2000 an outbreak killed spruce across 1.19 million ha of Alaskan forest, roughly 40 per cent more than the previous 70 years together [@Werner_2006], and a new outbreak under way since about 2016 has spread from the Susitna lowlands toward the Alaska Range [@Zwieback_2024]. Knowing where, when and how severely beetles kill spruce is needed for hazard management, for carbon accounting and for understanding how a warming climate changes boreal disturbance [@Hicke_2024; @Patacca_2022; @Morris_2016], yet the operational damage record for Alaska rests on aerial sketch mapping, whose polygons record only what an observer saw that year and understate dispersed low-severity mortality [@Zwieback_2024].

Satellite remote sensing gives the continuous record that survey flights cannot, in that four decades of Landsat observation at stand scale [@Wulder_2019], read through segmentation algorithms such as LandTrendr [@Kennedy_2010] or continuous change detection [@Zhu_2014], have produced a 25-year national record of disturbance [@White_2017] and separated defoliators from bark beetles [@Meigs_2011; @Senf_2015; @Meddens_2013], but these methods detect abrupt, stand-replacing disturbance reliably and lose skill on the partial, gradual change where most insect damage occurs [@Cohen_2017; @Senf_2017], so for bark beetles the established method maps the red and gray stages of heavily killed stands and low-severity dispersed mortality remains the recognised gap [@Hicke_2024; @Marvasti_Zadeh_2023].

The size of that gap in Alaska was measured by @Zwieback_2024, who mapped dead spruce at tree scale from 2 m WorldView-2 imagery with a convolutional network at 95 per cent average accuracy, and found that roughly 90 per cent of beetle-killed spruce in their Southcentral study area stood in stands of areal severity below 0.05, while stand-scale Landsat shortwave infrared change related clearly to severity only above 0.1, so in this mixed forest with low conifer fractions nearly all mortality lies below the detection floor of Landsat change analysis. High-resolution mapping fills that gap only with proprietary imagery [@Hart_2015; @Nowak_2026], Alaska-wide change attribution has relied on the same survey perimeters [@Pastick_2018], occurrence models predict beetle habitat rather than damage [@Zabihi_2021], and individual-tree mortality benchmarks exist only outside Alaska [@Khatri_Chhetri_2024].

Deep learning models that read the whole satellite time series, rather than the change in one spectral index between two dates, are the candidate method for detecting mortality below the 0.1 floor of Landsat change analysis, since one-dimensional convolutional networks [@Pelletier_2019] and self-attention models [@Ru_wurm_2020] classify satellite image time series without handcrafted temporal features [reviewed by @Miller_2024], and over the boreal forest of eastern Canada TempCNN and Transformer models on annual Landsat subsequences detected and dated partial and progressive disturbances that LandTrendr-based classification missed [@Perbet_2024], though whether that transfers from a defoliator in Quebec to a bark beetle in Alaska is unknown [@Kautz_2024]. The European literature on *Ips typographus* (Linnaeus, 1758) [@Abdullah_2018; @Huo_2021; @Dalponte_2022; @Candotti_2022] targets a tree that fades within one season, where *Dendroctonus*-attacked spruce fade over years, from green through red to gray [@Hicke_2024], so the signal here accumulates over time scales a monthly or annual series resolves, and the reference severity dataset that had been missing now exists in the tree-scale product of @Zwieback_2024, together with sub-metre statewide mosaics on which further labels can be digitised.

This study evaluates deep learning methods and a Sentinel-1 radar time series against that reference, and tests whether climate variables defined from the beetle's biology improve detection. It assembles a monthly Sentinel-1 radar series over Southcentral Alaska from June 2017, trains subsequence models [after @Perbet_2024] against stand-scale severity reference data, and measures them against the published shortwave infrared floor [@Zwieback_2024]. The objectives are to (1) quantify the skill with which a Sentinel-1 radar time series estimates stand-scale areal severity of beetle-associated mortality, reported per severity stratum; (2) determine the detectability floor, the lowest severity stratum at which detection skill exceeds a pre-registered threshold, for each method; (3) estimate the year of mortality onset, supervised by onset intervals triangulated between the two label epochs, and quantify its lag relative to the reference record; (4) quantify the contribution of biologically motivated climate variables to detection skill; and (5) reconstruct the annual progression of the outbreak from its 2016 onset through the present across the Matanuska-Susitna Borough application extent, evaluating the reconstruction against the aerial survey archive.

Three hypotheses are tested over the whole outbreak record. Under the null (H0), temporal deep learning models do not exceed the skill of the shortwave infrared change baseline below areal severity of 0.1, and the detection floor of @Zwieback_2024 stands; under the alternative (H1), subsequence models achieve significantly higher detection skill than the baseline within the 0.01 to 0.10 severity stratum, lowering the floor at which freely available imagery can monitor spruce beetle mortality. Under H2, models trained with mortality-onset intervals triangulated between the 2020 and 2023 label epochs date onset more accurately than the same models trained on single-epoch labels. Under H3, models receiving annual climate channels, a summer warmth index anchored on the 17 °C univoltinism threshold [@Hansen_2001], winter minimum temperature, and lagged summer means [@Berg_2006], detect low-severity mortality better than spectrally identical models without them. Estimated onset years are expected to lag true onset by one to two years, as observed for gradual disturbances elsewhere in the boreal [@Perbet_2024], and the severity strata, skill metrics and decision thresholds were fixed by pre-registration before any outcome data were analysed.

The third hypothesis rests on the beetle's biology, and its climate variables are defined from three parts of the life cycle, the generation time, the manner of spread and the winter, so the Introduction closes on them. Adult flight in Southcentral Alaska begins in early June once ambient temperature exceeds 12.8 °C [@Holsten_2001], during the rapid cambial growth of white spruce [@Hard_1985b], and whether the brood then matures in one year or two is under direct temperature control acting on the fourth larval instar and the prepupa [@Hansen_2001b], the best stand-level predictor of the univoltine proportion being cumulative hours above 17 °C from 40 to 90 days after peak flight [@Hansen_2001]. The temperature that governs it is that of the phloem rather than the air, since two-year cycles developed on the north and west faces of standing boles at a mean phloem temperature of 10.6 °C while one-year cycles developed on the south faces of the same trees at 16.5 °C [@Werner_1985]. A warm summer therefore halves the generation time without raising fecundity, and the shorter generation is what raises the rate of spruce mortality in an established outbreak [@Hansen_2003], while an obligate adult diapause requiring cold holds the life cycle to one year or longer [@Bleiker_2019; @Davenport_2024], so the mortality a satellite series records cannot advance faster than an annual increment however warm the summer.

Spread occurs by threshold and by opportunity rather than along a front, because pheromone-mediated aggregation raises attack density until it suffices to kill the host [@Jenkins_2014], so mortality accumulates in foci around killed trees, and attack succeeds where host defence is overwhelmed and growth is slow, since diameter predicted susceptibility only with slower than average radial growth over the previous five years [@Hard_1983; @Hard_1985]. Populations build in windthrown and weakened hosts before erupting onto standing stands [@Reynolds_1994], and the eruption is synchronous rather than radial, at many locations at once and synchronised by regional drivers, with beetle activity correlated only within about five kilometres [@Jenkins_2014; @Hart_2017], since beetles released in Alaska were recovered at most 600 m from their overwintering sites [@Werner_1997]. The regional driver is not temperature alone, because Colorado outbreaks were predicted best by drought [@Hart_2014] and initiated in summer, winter and multi-year drought marked by low peak snow water equivalent [@Hart_2017], while cold winters held Interior Alaska populations at endemic levels until those limits eased [@Holsten_1990], so the summer temperature relationship in the Alaskan record [@Berg_2006; @Sherriff_2011] holds together with a moisture term, and a population held at endemic level erupts when the limit eases, onto hosts already weakened.

The winter sets the last threshold, and it is a snow depth rather than an air temperature, because larvae and adults in Alaska supercooled to about −12 °C in summer and −31 °C in winter, neither stage was freeze tolerant, and temperatures beneath the bark of standing spruce showed that only beetles hibernating below the snow line would survive a typical winter [@Miller_1987], which is why attack concentrates on the lower bole [@Hard_1985b]. Winter minimum air temperature therefore bounds survival only for brood above the snow, the snowpack that shelters the brood is the one whose low peak water equivalent marked the drought-initiated outbreaks of the Southern Rockies [@Hart_2017], and snow depth over a stand follows elevation, canopy closure and terrain, all of which the analysis grid carries, so the overwintering threshold is a height on the bole rather than a temperature in the air, and the climate the models received was measured from that height.

# Materials and methods

## Study area

The study area encompasses the Southcentral Alaska outbreak region, centred on the Susitna lowlands and the Matanuska-Susitna Valley and bounded by the Talkeetna Mountains and the Alaska Range. Forests are boreal mosaics of white spruce (*Picea glauca* (Moench) Voss), black spruce (*P. mariana* (Mill.) Britton et al.), Alaska birch (*Betula neoalaskana* Sarg.) and trembling aspen (*Populus tremuloides* Michx.), with wetlands and mixed stands in which conifer fractions of 10 to 30% predominate, and the outbreak reached the area around 2016 and had exhausted much of the large white spruce by 2021 [@Zwieback_2024]. The nearest precedent occurred in the Kenai Peninsula during the outbreak of 1987 to 2000 [@Boucher_2006; @Roynolds_1996]. Three datasets fix the extents the study works within, the severity reference, the crown labels it was built from and the aerial survey record, and the chunks below define every extent once, on WGS 84 UTM zone 5N, the grid of the severity reference.

```{r}
#| label: extents
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# Every spatial extent the study uses, defined once, all on WGS 84 UTM zone 5N.
crs_utm <- "EPSG:32605"
albers_km <- paste("+proj=aea +lat_1=55 +lat_2=65 +lat_0=50 +lon_0=-154 +x_0=0",
                   "+y_0=0 +datum=NAD83 +units=km +no_defs")

# Independent severity reference, Zwieback (UAF) 2021, 90 m, no licence declared,
# evaluation only. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8423568. Its bounding box is
# the frame the block sample was drawn around, but it holds values on one strip
# along the Parks Highway, so the reference extent is the traced outline of its
# valid cells and the two are kept apart.
sev_ref <- terra::rast("02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c90c.tif")
stopifnot(terra::crs(sev_ref, describe = T)$code == "32605")
sev_bbox <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(sev_ref)))
sev_extent <- terra::ifel(is.na(sev_ref), NA, 1) |>
  terra::as.polygons(dissolve = T, na.rm = T) |>
  sf::st_as_sf() |> sf::st_geometry() |> sf::st_union() |>
  sf::st_sf(geometry = _)
stopifnot(abs(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sev_extent)) -
              sum(!is.na(terra::values(sev_ref))) * prod(terra::res(sev_ref))) < 1e4)

# The block sampling window: the reference bounding box padded by 50 km, as
# locked on 2026-08-12 (commit 0d5de75).
sample_window <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(sev_bbox, 50000))))

# Study area: Matanuska-Susitna Borough (Natural Earth 10 m). Retrieval link and
# date to be recorded in 02.inputs/README.md.
matsu <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/context/naturalearth.gpkg", "matsu_borough", quiet = T) |>
  sf::st_transform(crs_utm)

# Map, hillshade and context frame: the borough and the sampling window, padded by 15 km.
aoi <- sf::st_as_sf(sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(sf::st_buffer(
  sf::st_union(sf::st_geometry(matsu), sf::st_geometry(sample_window)), 15000))))

# Crown label tiles the published network was trained and tested on,
# https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10569990, CC-BY 4.0.
tile_files <- list.files("02.inputs/zwieback-labels", "_extent[.]gpkg$",
                         recursive = T, full.names = T)
tiles <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tile_files, function(f)
  sf::st_sf(set = ifelse(grepl("gpkg_validation", f), "validation", "training"),
            geometry = sf::st_geometry(sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(f, quiet = T), crs_utm)))))

# Aerial detection survey polygons for spruce beetle, 2016 onward, within the frame.
# USFS FHP Region 10, public domain.
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
ids <- sf::st_read(
  "02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", quiet = T,
  query = paste("SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, Shape FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10",
                "WHERE SURVEY_YEAR >= 2016 AND DCA_CODE IN (11009,80007)"),
  wkt_filter = sf::st_as_text(sf::st_transform(sf::st_geometry(aoi), 3338))) |>
  sf::st_transform(crs_utm)

meridian <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_sfc(
  sf::st_linestring(cbind(-150, seq(58, 66, 0.1))), crs = 4326)) |>
  sf::st_transform(crs_utm)
```

```{r}
#| label: studyarea-context
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# Rivers, roads and places for the map (Natural Earth 10 m; United States Census
# Bureau TIGER places), and a hillshade from the Amazon Web Services Terrain Tiles,
# https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/, whose source north of 60 degrees is
# the ArcticDEM 5 m mosaic, at zoom 10, about 76 m at this latitude; built once.
ctx_gpkg <- "02.inputs/derived/studyarea_context.gpkg"
hill_tif <- "02.inputs/covariates/hillshade_terraintiles_z10.tif"
if (!file.exists(ctx_gpkg)) {
  within_aoi <- function(layer, crs) sf::st_read(
    "02.inputs/context/naturalearth.gpkg", layer, quiet = T,
    wkt_filter = sf::st_as_text(sf::st_transform(sf::st_geometry(aoi), crs))) |>
    sf::st_transform(crs_utm)
  riv <- within_aoi("rivers", 4326)
  rds <- within_aoi("roads", 4326)
  plc <- within_aoi("places_census", 4269) |>
    subset(name %in% c("Cantwell", "Talkeetna", "Petersville", "Skwentna",
                       "Willow", "Sutton-Alpine", "Wasilla", "Palmer"))
  for (nm in c("riv", "rds", "plc"))
    sf::st_write(get(nm), ctx_gpkg, layer = nm, delete_layer = T, quiet = T)
}
if (!file.exists(hill_tif)) {
  dem <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(aoi, z = 10, clip = "locations", verbose = F) |>
    terra::rast() |> terra::crop(terra::vect(aoi))
  terra::writeRaster(dem, sub("hillshade", "dem", hill_tif), overwrite = T)
  terra::shade(terra::terrain(dem, "slope",  unit = "radians"),
               terra::terrain(dem, "aspect", unit = "radians"),
               angle = 40, direction = 315) |>
    terra::writeRaster(hill_tif, overwrite = T)
}
# MERIT Hydro upstream drainage area (Yamazaki et al. 2019, CC-BY 4.0), 90 m over the
# sampling window, fetched once from Earth Engine; channels draining 25 km2 or more
# are the rivers the map draws, and the landscape variables below read the same file.
merit_upa <- "02.inputs/covariates/landscape/merit_upa_90m.tif"
if (!file.exists(merit_upa)) {
  dir.create(dirname(merit_upa), showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
  win84 <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(sample_window, 4326))
  url <- ee$Image("MERIT/Hydro/v1_0_1")$select("upa")$toFloat()$getDownloadURL(list(
    region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(win84[["xmin"]], win84[["ymin"]], win84[["xmax"]], win84[["ymax"]])),
    scale = 90, crs = "EPSG:32605", format = "GEO_TIFF"))
  old <- options(timeout = 900); download.file(url, paste0(merit_upa, ".part"), mode = "wb", quiet = T); options(old)
  file.rename(paste0(merit_upa, ".part"), merit_upa)
}
rivers90 <- terra::ifel(terra::rast(merit_upa) >= 25, 1, NA)
ctx  <- function(layer) sf::st_read(ctx_gpkg, layer, quiet = T)
hill <- terra::rast(hill_tif)

tile_side <- function(set) round(sqrt(median(as.numeric(sf::st_area(tiles[tiles$set == set, ])))), -1)
studyarea_cap <- paste0(
  "Study area at a scale of 1:850,000. The yellow area outlined in red covers ",
  round(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sev_extent)) / 1e6), " km² where Zwieback et al. (2024) ",
  "mapped the severity of spruce beetle damage, between the Susitna River and the Parks ",
  "Highway west of Talkeetna. The black squares mark the ", nrow(tiles), " tiles in which ",
  "that study drew dead spruce crowns by hand, ", sum(tiles$set == "training"),
  " training tiles about ", tile_side("training"), " m across and ",
  sum(tiles$set == "validation"), " validation tiles about ", tile_side("validation"),
  " m across. The squares are drawn larger than the tiles so that they can be seen. ",
  "The pink areas are spruce beetle damage recorded by the aerial detection survey from ",
  min(ids$SURVEY_YEAR), " to ", max(ids$SURVEY_YEAR), ". The inset shows where the study ",
  "area lies in Alaska.")
```

The disturbance severity reference of @Zwieback_2024, the only stand-scale map of this outbreak, holds values on a `r round(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sev_extent)) / 1e6)` km² strip between the Susitna River and the Parks Highway from Talkeetna to Byers Lake, the cloud-free part of a 1,403 km² WorldView-2 image of 2 August 2021, and was held for evaluation alone. The `r nrow(tiles)` tiles on which that study hand-delineated dead crowns, `r sum(tiles$set == "training")` of 0.5 km and `r sum(tiles$set == "validation")` of 0.1 km, lie along the same corridor from Cantwell to Willow and tuned the crown network. The aerial detection survey record, `r min(ids$SURVEY_YEAR)` to `r max(ids$SURVEY_YEAR)` here, stratified the sample. The Matanuska-Susitna Borough, `r format(round(as.numeric(sf::st_area(matsu)) / 1e6), big.mark = ",")` km², was the extent of the wall-to-wall maps, and @fig-studyarea draws all of it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-studyarea-maps
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
#| fig-cap: !expr studyarea_cap
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.6

# Two maps for one figure. (a) Spruce beetle damage recorded by the aerial detection
# survey, USFS FHP Region 10,
# https://www.fs.usda.gov/foresthealth/docs/IDS_Data_for_Download/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb.zip
# (b) The study area at 1:1,000,000: the tiles of the Zwieback et al. (2024) crown labels,
# https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10569990, and the valid extent of their severity raster,
# https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8423568. Map (b) is saved at exactly half the figure,
# 3.5 by 5.6 inches, and placed at that size, so its scale holds when printed. Its frame
# is the map panel measured in that saved image, 2.98 by 4.575 inches, shifted 10 km
# east so the legend box clears most tiles. Delete the PNG to redraw it.

# Survey polygon count per year, read once.
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/survey_spread.csv")) {
  sf_use_s2(FALSE)
```

The aerial detection survey has recorded spruce beetle damage in Alaska since 1997, and @fig-outbreak draws its whole span. Across `r nrow(spread_yr)` survey years the area-weighted mean latitude of recorded damage moved north by `r sprintf("%.2f", coef(spread_fit)[2] * diff(range(spread_yr$year)))` degrees, about `r sprintf("%.0f", coef(spread_fit)[2] * diff(range(spread_yr$year)) * 111)` km \[F(1, `r spread_fit$df.residual`) = `r sprintf("%.2f", summary(spread_fit)$fstatistic[1])`, p = `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(spread_fit)$coefficients[2, 4])`, R² = `r sprintf("%.3f", summary(spread_fit)$r.squared)`\], a drift rather than a march, since the trend explained under a quarter of the variance and the mass at the start of the record is the Kenai Peninsula outbreak while the mass at the end is the Susitna lowlands. The polygons were not used as labels, because positional accuracy is coarse, low-severity damage is under-recorded and the intensity attribute, faded trees per treed area, is not commensurable with pixel-fraction severity [@Zwieback_2024]; they stratified the block sample by damage history and, through the flown-area footprints, separated surveyed absence from non-survey, with the annual counts tabulated below.

```{r}
#| label: ids-context
#| echo: true
ids_sql <- function(sql) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  gdal_utils("vectortranslate", "02.inputs/ids-region10/AK_Region10_AllYears.gdb", tmp,
             options = c("-dialect", "SQLite", "-sql", sql))
  read.csv(tmp)
}
sb <- ids_sql('
  SELECT SURVEY_YEAR, DCA_CODE, DCA_COMMON_NAME,
         COUNT(*) AS n_polygons, SUM(ACRES) AS acres
  FROM DAMAGE_AREAS_FLAT_AllYears_AK_Rgn10
  WHERE DCA_COMMON_NAME LIKE "%spruce beetle%"
  GROUP BY SURVEY_YEAR, DCA_CODE')
aggregate(cbind(n_polygons = sb$n_polygons, hectares = round(sb$acres * 0.40468564)),
          by = list(agent = sb$DCA_COMMON_NAME), FUN = sum)
data.frame(year = sb$SURVEY_YEAR[sb$DCA_CODE == 11009],
           n_polygons = sb$n_polygons[sb$DCA_CODE == 11009],
           hectares = round(sb$acres[sb$DCA_CODE == 11009] * 0.40468564))
```

Dead spruce in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough of Southcentral Alaska were mapped from the monthly Sentinel-1 radar record beginning in 2017, trained and tested on the crowns that @Zwieback_2024 digitised from WorldView-2 imagery of 2021, and the accuracy reached was compared with that of their published map. The research design section describes those crown labels, their split into training and test data and the 10 m cells the models were fitted on. The environmental variables section describes the radar record and the climate, terrain and landscape variables, and the models and assessment section describes how the temporal convolutional network was tuned and how its accuracy was tested against @Zwieback_2024. All inputs were publicly available and were retrieved and processed by the code shown in this manuscript.

## Reference data

Stand-scale areal severity of beetle-associated dead spruce for the Talkeetna to Byers Lake area in 2021, derived by @Zwieback_2024 from a convolutional network applied to WorldView-2 imagery and therefore a model product with its own documented error rather than ground truth, was used at its three released stand scales solely for independent evaluation, and its metadata alone were inspected before pre-registration.

```{r}
#| label: severity-metadata
#| echo: false
sev <- lapply(sprintf("02.inputs/zwieback-severity/merged_ref_h_c%sc.tif", c(30, 90, 250)), rast)
data.frame(
  file = vapply(sev, function(r) basename(sources(r)), ""),
  resolution = vapply(sev, function(r) paste(round(res(r)), collapse = " x "), ""),
  ncell = vapply(sev, ncell, numeric(1)),
  crs = vapply(sev, function(r) st_crs(crs(r))$Name, "")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: label-numbers
#| echo: false
#| output: false
pairs <- read.csv("03.outputs/label_pairs.csv")
crown_m <- read.csv("03.outputs/crown_net_metrics.csv")
best <- crown_m[which.max(crown_m$val_iou), ]
op <- read.csv("03.outputs/crown_operating_point.csv")
tq <- read.csv("03.outputs/triage_queue.csv")
```

Reference labels were dead spruce crowns digitised over the 160 blocks on the State of Alaska mosaics of 2020, at 0.5 m, and 2023, at 0.3 m, licensed Maxar imagery processed locally and never redistributed, the study publishing only the derived crowns and severity fractions as @Zwieback_2024 did. Labelling followed @Zwieback_2024 for pre-labelling and @Khatri_Chhetri_2024 for triage. Their released dead-spruce network was adapted from seven WorldView-2 bands to the mosaics' four and fine-tuned on their `r format(sum(pairs$crowns), big.mark = ",")` published crowns over `r nrow(pairs)` areas, the best epoch on held-out areas reaching a pixel recall of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_recall)` at a precision of `r sprintf("%.2f", best$val_precision)`; its candidates were refined into polygons with DeepForest [@Weinstein_2019] and the Segment Anything Model [@Wu_2023] and written per block and epoch at a probability of 0.5, `r format(sum(tq$candidates), big.mark = ",")` polygons at a median of `r median(tq$candidates)` per block, for annotation in QGIS. Accepted crowns were rasterised to the fraction of each 10 m cell they cover, the areal severity, and the two epochs gave each crown a state, dead by 2020, died between 2020 and 2023, or alive through 2023, which supplied the interval-censored onset labels. The published crowns joined the training pool within their own areas, the severity rasters took no part in labelling, mortality agent was inferred from context, and dead spruce under closed deciduous canopy are absent; the tuning pairs, the network and the queue are in the supplement.

```{r}
#| label: sample-blocks
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# The 160 blocks of 512 m locked on 2026-08-12. Candidate
# blocks tile the sampling window; those with conifer cover of 5 per cent or more
# (ABoVE top cover 2020, Macander and Nelson 2022, https://doi.org/10.3334/ORNLDAAC/2032)
# were stratified by cover tercile and by surveyed damage since 2016 and drawn in
# proportion with a floor of ten per stratum. The file exists, so the drawing code
# is skipped; the folds are dealt under Spatial folds once the variables exist.
block_gpkg <- "02.inputs/derived/sample_blocks.gpkg"
if (!file.exists(block_gpkg)) {
  set.seed(20260811)
  g <- terra::rast(terra::ext(terra::vect(sample_window)), resolution = 512, crs = crs_utm)
  terra::values(g) <- seq_len(terra::ncell(g))
  cand <- sf::st_as_sf(terra::as.polygons(g, dissolve = F))
  cand$conifer <- terra::values(terra::project(
    terra::rast("02.inputs/covariates/conifer_topcover_2020.tif"), g, method = "average"),
    mat = F)
  cand$damage <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(cand, ids)) > 0
  bl <- cand[!is.na(cand$conifer) & cand$conifer >= 5, ]
  bl$stratum <- paste0("c", cut(bl$conifer, quantile(bl$conifer, c(0, 1/3, 2/3, 1)),
                                include.lowest = T, labels = 1:3), "_d", as.integer(bl$damage))
  tab   <- table(bl$stratum)
  alloc <- pmax(10, round(160 * as.numeric(tab) / sum(tab)))
  alloc <- setNames(round(alloc * 160 / sum(alloc)), names(tab))
  samp  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(tab), function(st) {
    x <- bl[bl$stratum == st, ]; x[sample(nrow(x), min(alloc[st], nrow(x))), ]
  }))
  sf::st_write(samp, block_gpkg, delete_dsn = T, quiet = T)
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(samp)))
  write.csv(data.frame(block_id = seq_len(nrow(samp)), x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2],
                       conifer = round(samp$conifer, 1), damage = samp$damage,
                       stratum = samp$stratum),
            sub("gpkg$", "csv", block_gpkg), row.names = F)
}
blocks <- sf::st_read(block_gpkg, quiet = T) |> transform(block = seq_along(conifer))
```

The `r nrow(blocks)` blocks of 512 m were drawn on 2026-08-12 from a `r format(round(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sample_window)) / 1e6), big.mark = ",")` km² window, the reference raster's bounding box padded by 50 km, and dealt to eight spatial folds by blockCV over hexagons sized by the measured autocorrelation range, under Environmental variables; `r sum(lengths(sf::st_intersects(blocks, sev_extent)) > 0)` blocks lie on the strip and models scored against the reference are trained without their folds.

```{r}
#| label: stand-cells
#| echo: true
#| output: false
strata <- c(0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1)
strata_lab <- c("0-0.01", "0.01-0.03", "0.03-0.05", "0.05-0.10", "0.10-0.20", ">0.20")
RES <- 10; NCELL <- 76
if (!file.exists("02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.gpkg")) {
  eq7 <- st_transform(blocks, "EPSG:27705")
  cells10 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(eq7)), function(i) {
    bb <- st_bbox(eq7[i, ])
    x0 <- round(mean(bb[c("xmin", "xmax")]) / RES) * RES - (NCELL / 2) * RES
    y1 <- round(mean(bb[c("ymin", "ymax")]) / RES) * RES + (NCELL / 2) * RES
    r <- rast(nrows = NCELL, ncols = NCELL, xmin = x0, xmax = x0 + NCELL * RES,
              ymin = y1 - NCELL * RES, ymax = y1, crs = "EPSG:27705")
    values(r) <- 1; r[c(1, NCELL), ] <- NA; r[, c(1, NCELL)] <- NA
    p <- st_as_sf(as.polygons(r, dissolve = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE))
    inside <- st_within(st_centroid(st_geometry(p)), st_geometry(eq7[i, ]), sparse = FALSE)[, 1]
    st_sf(block = eq7$block[i], geometry = st_geometry(p[inside, ]))
  }))
  cells10$id <- seq_len(nrow(cells10))
  for (epoch in c(2020, 2023)) {
    cells10[[paste0("sev_", epoch)]] <- 0
    for (b in unique(cells10$block)) {
      cr <- st_read(sprintf("02.inputs/prelabels/%d/block_%03d.gpkg", epoch, b), quiet = TRUE)
      if (!nrow(cr)) next
      i <- which(cells10$block == b)
      a <- st_intersection(st_sf(id = i, geometry = st_geometry(cells10[i, ])),
                           st_transform(st_union(cr), "EPSG:27705"))
      area <- tapply(as.numeric(st_area(a)), a$id, sum)
      cells10[[paste0("sev_", epoch)]][as.integer(names(area))] <- area / RES^2
    }
  }
  cells10$stratum <- cut(cells10$sev_2023, strata, strata_lab, include.lowest = TRUE)
  st_write(cells10, "02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)
  xy <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_geometry(cells10)))
  write.csv(data.frame(st_drop_geometry(cells10), x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2]),
            "02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.csv", row.names = FALSE)
}
cells10 <- read.csv("02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_10m.csv")
cells10$stratum <- factor(cells10$stratum, strata_lab)
cell_n <- table(cells10$stratum)
```

The sample unit was the 10 m Equi7Grid cell the radar record is held on, entering when its centre lay inside a block and outside the outer ring the speckle filter leaves empty, `r format(nrow(cells10), big.mark = ",")` cells over the 160 blocks. Until the triage queue is annotated the labels are the machine candidates at a probability of 0.5, dissolved to the fraction of each cell they cover in each epoch, the 2023 fraction placing `r format(cell_n[["0-0.01"]], big.mark = ",")` cells below 0.01 and `r format(sum(cell_n) - cell_n[["0-0.01"]], big.mark = ",")` at or above it, `r format(sum(cell_n[c("0.01-0.03", "0.03-0.05", "0.05-0.10")]), big.mark = ",")` of them in the 0.01 to 0.10 stratum the first hypothesis is scored in; every result on these labels is the seed round of the annotation design and is reported as such.

```{r}

#| echo: true

                       sf::st_drop_geometry(mtbs[mtbs$year >= 2017, ]), sum)
```

## Predictor variables

Daily minimum and maximum air temperature from the Daymet version 4 gridded forcings at 1 km [@Thornton_2021], the record standing nearest to the phloem temperature and the snow depth the biology named, were reduced per 90 m stand cell and year to three variables, the summer warmth index, the cumulative degree-hours above 17 °C from June through September, a fixed-window form of the univoltinism predictor of @Hansen_2001; the winter minimum, the lowest daily minimum from November through March, the cold to which brood above the snow line is exposed [@Werner_2006; @Bentz_2010]; and the lagged summer mean, the mean summer temperature two years earlier, following the lagged association in the regional outbreak record [@Berg_2006; @Sherriff_2011].

```{r}
#| label: climate-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
series_csv  <- "02.inputs/derived/climate_series.csv"
monthly_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/climate_monthly.csv"
annual_tif  <- function(y) sprintf("02.inputs/climate/clim_%d.tif", y)
monthly_tif <- function(y) sprintf("02.inputs/climate/monthly/clim_m_%d.tif", y)
dir.create("02.inputs/climate/monthly", recursive = T, showWarnings = F)
dir.create("02.inputs/derived", showWarnings = F)

need_series  <- !file.exists(series_csv) ||
  max(readr::read_csv(series_csv, show_col_types = F)$year) < 2025
todo_annual  <- (2012:2025)[!file.exists(annual_tif(2012:2025))]
todo_monthly <- (2017:2025)[!file.exists(monthly_tif(2017:2025))]

if (need_series || !file.exists(monthly_csv) || length(c(todo_annual, todo_monthly))) {
  invisible(reticulate::py_capture_output(
  	rgee::ee_Initialize(project = "murphys-deforisk", quiet = T), type = "stderr"))
	ee <- rgee::ee
  dm <- ee$ImageCollection("NASA/ORNL/DAYMET_V4")

  rect_of <- function(x) {
    b <- terra::project(x, "EPSG:4326") |> terra::ext() |> as.vector()
    ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(b[1], b[3], b[2], b[4]))
  }
  tmean_of  <- function(ic) ic$map(function(im)
    im$select("tmax")$add(im$select("tmin"))$divide(2)$rename("tmean"))
  warmth_of <- function(ic) tmean_of(ic)$map(function(im)
    im$subtract(17)$max(0)$multiply(24))$sum()
  annual <- function(y) {
    smr <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-06-01", y), sprintf("%d-10-01", y))
    wtr <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-11-01", y - 1), sprintf("%d-04-01", y))
    warmth_of(smr)$rename("warmth")$
      addBands(tmean_of(smr)$mean()$rename("summer_mean"))$
      addBands(wtr$select("tmin")$min()$rename("winter_min"))
  }
  
  monthly <- function(y) ee$Image$cat(lapply(1:12, function(m) {
    d <- dm$filterDate(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", y, m),
                       sprintf("%d-%02d-01", y + (m == 12), m %% 12 + 1))
    ee$Image$cat(d$select("tmax")$mean(), d$select("tmin")$mean(),
                 warmth_of(d), d$select("prcp")$sum())$
      rename(sprintf(c("tmax_%02d", "tmin_%02d", "warmth_%02d", "prcp_%02d"), m))
  }))
  regional <- function(img, region) unlist(img$reduceRegion(
    reducer = ee$Reducer$mean(), geometry = region, scale = 1000, maxPixels = 1e10)$getInfo())
  fetch <- function(img, path, region) {
    url <- img$toFloat()$getDownloadURL(list(
      region = region, scale = 1000, crs = "EPSG:32605", format = "GEO_TIFF"))
    old <- options(timeout = 600); on.exit(options(old))
    download.file(url, paste0(path, ".part"), mode = "wb", quiet = T)
    file.rename(paste0(path, ".part"), path)
  }
  
  roi_a <- rect_of(terra::vect(sample_window))
  if (need_series) {
    clim <- data.frame(year = 1990:2025, do.call(rbind, lapply(1990:2025, function(y)
      regional(annual(y), roi_a))))
    clim$summer_mean_lag2 <- c(NA, NA, head(clim$summer_mean, -2))
    write.csv(clim, series_csv, row.names = F)
  }
  for (y in todo_annual) fetch(annual(y), annual_tif(y), roi_a)

  roi_m <- rect_of(terra::as.polygons(terra::ext(terra::rast(annual_tif(2016))),
                                      crs = "EPSG:32605"))
  if (!file.exists(monthly_csv)) {
    dm90 <- dm$filterDate("1990-01-01", "2026-01-01")
    days <- c(31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31)
    rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:12, function(m) {
      sub <- dm90$filter(ee$Filter$calendarRange(m, m, "month"))
      v   <- regional(sub$select(c("tmax", "tmin"))$mean()$
                        addBands(sub$select("prcp")$mean()$multiply(days[m])$rename("prcp")),
                      roi_m)
      data.frame(month = m, tmax = v[["tmax"]], tmin = v[["tmin"]], prcp = v[["prcp"]])
    }))
    rows$tmean <- (rows$tmax + rows$tmin) / 2
    write.csv(rows, monthly_csv, row.names = F)
  }
  for (y in todo_monthly) fetch(monthly(y), monthly_tif(y), roi_m)
}  

clim   <- readr::read_csv(series_csv, show_col_types = F)
clim_m <- readr::read_csv(monthly_csv, show_col_types = F) |>
  transform(month_name = month.abb[month])
warm_m <- clim_m[which.max(clim_m$tmax), ]

clim_names <- c("tmax", "tmin", "warmth", "prcp")
clim_stack <- terra::rast(
	lapply(2017:2025, function(y) {
		r <- terra::rast(monthly_tif(y))
		names(r) <- paste(rep(clim_names, 12), sprintf("%d-%02d-01", y, rep(1:12, each = 4)), sep = "_")
		r
}))
warmth_check <- terra::global(abs(
  sum(clim_stack[[paste0("warmth_2020-", sprintf("%02d", 6:9), "-01")]]) -
    terra::resample(terra::rast(annual_tif(2020))[[1]], clim_stack)), "max", na.rm = T)
stopifnot(warmth_check$max < 0.01)
```

@fig-climograph gives the seasonal setting, in which the warmest month, `r month.name[warm_m$month]`, had a mean daily maximum of `r sprintf("%.1f", warm_m$tmax)` °C over 1990 to 2025, below the 17 °C threshold, so degree-hours accrue only on the warmer days of the window and a summer a degree above normal shortens the generation [@Hansen_2001]; @fig-climate shows the three variables over 1990 to 2025.

```{r}
#| label: fig-climograph
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Climograph of the study area from Daymet version 4 daily forcings averaged over 1990 to 2025, monthly mean precipitation as bars against monthly mean, maximum and minimum daily air temperature. The horizontal line marks the 17 °C threshold above which spruce beetle development accrues toward a one-year generation, and the shaded band marks June through September, the window over which the summer warmth index integrates. Adult flight occurs in early summer, at the opening of that band."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.2
base <- floor(min(clim_m$tmin) / 5) * 5
sc   <- max(clim_m$prcp) / (max(clim_m$tmax) - base)
ggplot(clim_m, aes(x = month)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 5.5, xmax = 9.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "grey85", alpha = .55) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = month - 0.35, xmax = month + 0.35, ymin = base,
                ymax = base + prcp / sc), fill = "steelblue4", alpha = .75) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 17, linetype = "22", colour = "#C0392B") +
  annotate("text", x = 1.4, y = 18.2, label = "17 °C univoltinism threshold",
           size = 2.5, colour = "#C0392B", hjust = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmax,  colour = "Daily maximum"), linewidth = .5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmean, colour = "Daily mean"),    linewidth = .6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmin,  colour = "Daily minimum"), linewidth = .5) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("Daily maximum" = "#E67E22",
                                       "Daily mean"    = "grey20",
                                       "Daily minimum" = "steelblue4")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Temperature (°C)",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - base) * sc, name = "Precipitation (mm)")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = month.abb, expand = c(.01, .01)) +
  labs(x = NULL) + th + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-climate
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Annual climate variables over the study window from Daymet version 4 daily forcings, 1990 to 2025. (a) Summer warmth index, the cumulative degree-hours above 17 °C from June to September, the seasonal window in which development above the univoltinism threshold accrues. (b) Winter minimum daily temperature, November to March, when overwintering stages beneath the bark are exposed to cold mortality; the two-year lagged summer mean tracks the delayed population response. The dashed line marks the 2016 outbreak onset."
#| fig-width: 7

pa <- ggplot(clim, aes(year, warmth)) +

  geom_line(aes(y = winter_min,       colour = "Winter minimum"),        linewidth = .5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = summer_mean_lag2, colour = "Summer mean, lag 2 yr"), linewidth = .5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2016, linetype = "22", colour = "grey30") +

                                       "Summer mean, lag 2 yr" = "#E67E22")) +
  labs(title = "(b) Winter minimum and lagged summer mean", y = "°C", x = NULL) +
  th + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
pa / pb
```

```{r}
#| label: climate-variance
#| echo: false
#| output: false
if (!file.exists("03.outputs/climate_variance.csv")) {
  cf <- sort(list.files("02.inputs/climate", pattern = "^clim_[0-9]{4}[.]tif$", full.names = T))
  nm <- c("summer warmth index", "summer mean", "winter minimum")
  cv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:3, function(b) {
    st <- terra::rast(lapply(cf, function(x) terra::rast(x)[[b]]))
    v  <- terra::extract(st, terra::vect(sf::st_transform(blocks, terra::crs(st))),
                         fun = mean, na.rm = T, ID = F)
    v  <- v[complete.cases(v), ]
    data.frame(channel = nm[b], blocks = nrow(v), between_year = sd(colMeans(v)),
               between_block = mean(apply(v, 2, sd)))
  }))
  cv$ratio <- cv$between_year / cv$between_block
  write.csv(cv, "03.outputs/climate_variance.csv", row.names = F)
}
climvar <- readr::read_csv("03.outputs/climate_variance.csv", show_col_types = F)
cvr     <- function(ch) climvar$ratio[climvar$channel == ch]
```

Climate entered in two forms: the three annual channels of the third hypothesis, the summer warmth index, the winter minimum and the two-year lagged summer mean, and, under the amendment of 2026-09-09, four monthly channels on the radar's own step, the mean daily maximum, the mean daily minimum, the degree-hours above 17 °C and the precipitation total, from June 2017 to December 2025 where the Daymet record ends; the June to September degree-hours of the monthly series summed to the annual warmth index within `r format(signif(warmth_check$max, 1))` in every cell. Over the `r climvar$blocks[1]` blocks the ratio of a channel's variation between years to its variation between blocks within a year was `r sprintf("%.2f", cvr("summer warmth index"))` for the warmth index and `r sprintf("%.2f", cvr("winter minimum"))` for the winter minimum, channels that mark the year, and `r sprintf("%.2f", cvr("summer mean"))` for the summer mean, a channel that marks the place; Figure S1 draws the warmth index over the blocks in the warmest and the coolest year.

Terrain is the relief the radar was corrected for and the ground the brood overwinters on, the snow line following elevation, canopy and aspect. Elevation, slope, northness and eastness were built for every block from the ArcticDEM 5 m mosaic through the Amazon Web Services Terrain Tiles at zoom 14, its native resolution here, averaged to 11 m, one file per block with a virtual mosaic over all `r nrow(blocks)`. The blocks sit on the low relief of the Susitna lowlands, so no layover and shadow mask was applied to the radar record, an omission the Limitations record.

```{r}
#| label: terrain-build
#| echo: true
#| output: false
terrain_dir <- "02.inputs/covariates/terrain_z14"
dir.create(terrain_dir, showWarnings = F)
terrain_tif <- function(i) sprintf("%s/block_%03d.tif", terrain_dir, i)
for (i in blocks$block[!file.exists(terrain_tif(blocks$block))]) {
  dem <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(blocks[blocks$block == i, ], z = 14, clip = "bbox",
                                  expand = 100, verbose = F) |> terra::rast()
  aspect <- terra::terrain(dem, v = "aspect", unit = "radians", neighbors = 8)
  trn <- c(dem, terra::terrain(dem, v = "slope", unit = "degrees", neighbors = 8),
           cos(aspect), sin(aspect)) |>
    terra::aggregate(fact = 5, fun = "mean", na.rm = T)
  names(trn) <- c("elev", "slope", "northness", "eastness")
  terra::writeRaster(trn, terrain_tif(i), overwrite = T)
}
terra::vrt(list.files(terrain_dir, "^block_[0-9]{3}[.]tif$", full.names = T),
           file.path(terrain_dir, "terrain.vrt"), overwrite = T)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(terrain_tif(blocks$block))))
```

```{r}
#| label: landscape-build
#| echo: false
#| output: false
# Static landscape variables per 10 m stand cell, each from an open source with the
# retrieval scripted here and run once. Distances are Euclidean, in metres, from a
# 90 m distance raster over the sampling window; land cover is read at the cell.
static_csv <- "02.inputs/derived/stand_cells_static.csv"
lsd <- "02.inputs/covariates/landscape"
dir.create(lsd, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)
if (!file.exists(static_csv)) {
  win84 <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(sample_window, 4326))
  roi <- ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(win84[["xmin"]], win84[["ymin"]], win84[["xmax"]], win84[["ymax"]]))
  fetch <- function(img, path, scale, region = roi, crs = "EPSG:32605") {
    if (file.exists(path)) return(invisible(path))
    url <- img$toFloat()$getDownloadURL(list(region = region, scale = scale, crs = crs, format = "GEO_TIFF"))
    old <- options(timeout = 900); on.exit(options(old))
    download.file(url, paste0(path, ".part"), mode = "wb", quiet = T)
    file.rename(paste0(path, ".part"), path)
  }
  dist_of <- function(mask) mask$selfMask()$fastDistanceTransform(2048, "pixels", "squared_euclidean")$
    sqrt()$multiply(90)$reproject("EPSG:32605", NULL, 90)
  # MERIT Hydro (Yamazaki et al. 2019, CC-BY 4.0): upstream area upa in km2 and the
  # water mask wat. The drainage network is every cell draining at least 1 km2; the
  # lakes and rivers are the water mask and channels draining at least 25 km2.
  mh <- ee$Image("MERIT/Hydro/v1_0_1")$reproject("EPSG:32605", NULL, 90)
  fetch(dist_of(mh$select("upa")$gte(1)), file.path(lsd, "dist_drainage_90m.tif"), 90)
  fetch(dist_of(mh$select("wat")$eq(1)$Or(mh$select("upa")$gte(25))), file.path(lsd, "dist_lake_river_90m.tif"), 90)
  # TIGER 2016 roads (United States Census Bureau, public domain).
  roads <- ee$FeatureCollection("TIGER/2016/Roads")$filterBounds(roi)
  fetch(roads$distance(100000)$reproject("EPSG:32605", NULL, 90), file.path(lsd, "dist_road_90m.tif"), 90)
  # NLCD 2016 Alaska land cover, 30 m (United States Geological Survey, public domain),
  # one 10 m tile per block on UTM zone 5, since Earth Engine does not know the Equi7 code.
  nlcd <- ee$Image("USGS/NLCD_RELEASES/2016_REL/2016_AK")$select("landcover")
  for (i in blocks$block) {
    bb <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(blocks[blocks$block == i, ], 4326))
    fetch(nlcd, sprintf("%s/nlcd_block_%03d.tif", lsd, i), 10,
          region = ee$Geometry$Rectangle(c(bb[["xmin"]] - 0.01, bb[["ymin"]] - 0.005, bb[["xmax"]] + 0.01, bb[["ymax"]] + 0.005)))
  }
  # Distance to coastline (Natural Earth 10 m) and to settlements (Census Bureau
  # TIGER places), rasterised at 90 m over the window and distance-transformed.
  tpl90 <- terra::rast(file.path(lsd, "dist_drainage_90m.tif"))
  coast <- rnaturalearth::ne_coastline(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf") |> sf::st_transform(32605)
  towns <- sf::st_read("02.inputs/context/naturalearth.gpkg", "places_census", quiet = T) |> sf::st_transform(32605)
  big <- terra::rast(terra::ext(tpl90) + 400000, resolution = 90, crs = "EPSG:32605")
  for (nm in c("coast", "town")) {
    v <- terra::vect(if (nm == "coast") coast else towns)
    r <- terra::rasterize(v, big, field = 1, background = NA)
    d <- terra::distance(r) |> terra::crop(tpl90)
    terra::writeRaster(d, sprintf("%s/dist_%s_90m.tif", lsd, nm), overwrite = T)
  }
  # Read every variable at the cell centre.
  pts <- terra::vect(cells10[, c("x", "y")], geom = c("x", "y"), crs = "EPSG:27705")
  pts5 <- terra::project(pts, "EPSG:32605")
  at <- function(r, p) terra::extract(r, p, ID = F)[, 1]
  static <- data.frame(id = cells10$id, block = cells10$block,
    elev = NA_real_, slope = NA_real_, northness = NA_real_, eastness = NA_real_,
    conifer = at(terra::rast("02.inputs/covariates/conifer_topcover_2020.tif"), terra::project(pts, terra::crs(terra::rast("02.inputs/covariates/conifer_topcover_2020.tif")))),
    landcover = NA_integer_,
    dist_drainage = at(terra::rast(file.path(lsd, "dist_drainage_90m.tif")), pts5),
    dist_lake_river = at(terra::rast(file.path(lsd, "dist_lake_river_90m.tif")), pts5),
    dist_coast = at(terra::rast(file.path(lsd, "dist_coast_90m.tif")), pts5),
    dist_road = at(terra::rast(file.path(lsd, "dist_road_90m.tif")), pts5),
    dist_town = at(terra::rast(file.path(lsd, "dist_town_90m.tif")), pts5))
  for (i in blocks$block) {
    k <- which(cells10$block == i)
    trn <- terra::rast(sprintf("02.inputs/covariates/terrain_z14/block_%03d.tif", i))
    static[k, c("elev", "slope", "northness", "eastness")] <- terra::extract(trn, terra::project(pts[k], terra::crs(trn)), ID = F)
    static$landcover[k] <- at(terra::rast(sprintf("%s/nlcd_block_%03d.tif", lsd, i)), pts5[k])
  }
  write.csv(static, static_csv, row.names = F)
}
static <- read.csv(static_csv)
stopifnot(nrow(static) == nrow(cells10), all(static$id == cells10$id))
static_na <- colSums(is.na(static))
```

The landscape a cell sits in entered as `r ncol(static) - 2` static variables read at the cell centre: elevation, slope, northness and eastness from the terrain built above; conifer cover from the ABoVE top-cover map [@Macander_2022]; land cover from the 2016 National Land Cover Database for Alaska; and five Euclidean distances, to the drainage network and to lakes and rivers from MERIT Hydro, to the coastline, to roads and to settlements, the distances following the design of @Zabihi_2021 and the drainage network entering because beetle populations build in the riparian stands where windthrow and slow growth first weaken hosts [@Reynolds_1994; @Hard_1983].

```{r}
#| label: radar-record-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
s1_scenes <- read.csv("03.outputs/s1_rtc_scene_means.csv")
seen <- lapply(split(s1_scenes$block, s1_scenes$track), unique)
s1_blocks <- c(only_131 = length(setdiff(seen[["131"]], seen[["160"]])),
               both = length(intersect(seen[["131"]], seen[["160"]])),
               only_160 = length(setdiff(seen[["160"]], seen[["131"]])))
s1_nscene <- tapply(s1_scenes$scene_id, s1_scenes$track, function(x) length(unique(x)))
s1_first <- min(as.Date(s1_scenes$date[s1_scenes$track == 131]))
s1_floor30 <- read.csv("03.outputs/radar_noise_floor_undamaged_10m.csv")
s1_ref <- read.csv("03.outputs/radar_noise_floor.csv")
floor30 <- function(what, b, p)
  s1_floor30[[what]][s1_floor30$processing == p & s1_floor30$band == b]
ref_db <- function(q) s1_ref$value[s1_ref$quantity == q]
yr_floor <- function(b, p = "mt_filtered") floor30("year_to_year_median_db", b, p)
rep_floor <- function(b, p = "mt_filtered") floor30("repeatability_median_db", b, p)
removed <- function(b) 100 * (1 - yr_floor(b) / yr_floor(b, "unfiltered"))
canopy_ratio <- c(VV = ref_db("windthrow_vv_db") / yr_floor("VV"),
                  VH = ref_db("windthrow_vh_db") / yr_floor("VH"))
s1val <- read.csv("03.outputs/s1gbm_validation.csv")
s1_cube_files <- list.files("02.inputs/derived/s1_cube_10m",
                            pattern = "^SENTINEL-1_RTC_.*[.]tif$")
s1_cube_dates <- as.Date(unique(regmatches(
  s1_cube_files, regexpr("[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}", s1_cube_files))))
```

The predictor record was Sentinel-1 C-band radar over the 160 blocks from June 2017, in VV, sent and received vertically, and VH, received horizontally, which returns more from the canopy; radar passes the cloud that limits optical observation here, so the step was monthly where the optical record was annual. Scenes came from the Planetary Computer's terrain corrected collection, `sentinel-1-rtc`, in which the return is corrected for the slope and aspect of the ground [@Small_2011], at 10 m sampling, and from orbit 131 alone, which saw every block, `r s1_blocks[["only_131"]]` alone and `r s1_blocks[["both"]]` with orbit 160, which saw `r s1_blocks[["only_160"]]` alone; the record began on `r format(s1_first, "%d %B %Y")`, earlier scenes carrying VV alone, and holds `r s1_nscene[["131"]]` scenes. Each scene was reprojected once, by area-weighted average, onto the 10 m Equi7Grid North America (EPSG:27705), the grid the Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model is distributed on, so the record crosses the seam between UTM zones 5 and 6 without one; the comparison against Earth Engine's uncorrected collection is in the supplement.

The whole radar chain is the two chunks that follow. The first reads every scene of orbit 131 through the Planetary Computer's STAC catalogue, reprojects each block's window once, caches one array per scene and reshuffles the cache into one memory-mapped array per block, a whole stack at 10 m being 5.6 GB on an 8 GB machine. The second applies the multi-temporal speckle filter of @Quegan_2000, in which each date keeps its own 3 by 3 local mean, the ratios of every image to its local mean are averaged across all dates and each date's mean is multiplied back, so change between dates stays while the speckle, the grainy noise of a radar image, cancels across the stack, as @fig-filter shows for one block on one date; every date was kept because the filter takes its noise reduction from the length of the series.

```{python}
#| label: radar-extract
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import argparse
import datetime as dt
import json
import os
import threading
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

os.environ.update({
    "GDAL_DISABLE_READDIR_ON_OPEN": "EMPTY_DIR",
    "GDAL_HTTP_MULTIPLEX": "YES", "GDAL_HTTP_VERSION": "2",
    "VSI_CACHE": "TRUE", "VSI_CACHE_SIZE": "16777216", "GDAL_CACHEMAX": "32",
})
import numpy as np
import rasterio
# The R session this runs in sets PROJ_LIB to an R package's own PROJ database,
# which rasterio's PROJ cannot read, so point it at the system PROJ data.
import rasterio._env
try:
    import pyproj
    _proj = pyproj.datadir.get_data_dir()
except ImportError:
    _proj = next((d for d in ("/opt/local/lib/proj9/share/proj", "/opt/local/share/proj",
                              "/usr/local/share/proj", "/usr/share/proj")
                  if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, "proj.db"))), None)
if _proj:
    os.environ["PROJ_LIB"] = os.environ["PROJ_DATA"] = _proj
    rasterio._env.set_proj_data_search_path(_proj)
import geopandas as gpd
from rasterio.crs import CRS
from rasterio.enums import Resampling
from rasterio.transform import from_origin
from rasterio.warp import reproject, transform_bounds
from rasterio.windows import Window, from_bounds

ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "02.inputs").is_dir())
BLOCKS = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "sample_blocks.gpkg"
CACHE = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_scene_cache_10m"
OUTDIR = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_blocks_10m"
STAC = "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/stac/v1/search"
SAS = "https://planetarycomputer.microsoft.com/api/sas/v1/token/sentinel-1-rtc"
BBOX = [-151.963, 61.52, -148.438, 63.467]
TRACK, RES, NCELL = 131, 10, 76
DST = CRS.from_epsg(27705)
_tok = {"v": None, "e": 0.0}
_lock = threading.Lock()

def token():
    with _lock:
        if time.time() < _tok["e"] - 300:
            return _tok["v"]
        with urllib.request.urlopen(SAS, timeout=60) as f:
            d = json.load(f)
        _tok["v"] = d["token"]
        exp = d.get("msft:expiry")
        _tok["e"] = (dt.datetime.fromisoformat(exp.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
                     if exp else time.time() + 3300)
        return _tok["v"]

def scenes_on_track():
    body = {"collections": ["sentinel-1-rtc"], "bbox": BBOX,
            "datetime": "2017-06-03T00:00:00Z/2026-12-31T23:59:59Z",
            "query": {"sat:orbit_state": {"eq": "descending"},
                      "sat:relative_orbit": {"eq": TRACK}}, "limit": 500}
    out = []
    while True:
        req = urllib.request.Request(STAC, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                     headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as f:
            page = json.load(f)
        feats = page.get("features", [])
        for it in feats:
            p, a = it["properties"], it.get("assets", {})
            pols = p.get("sar:polarizations") or []
            if "VV" not in pols or "VH" not in pols or "vv" not in a or "vh" not in a:
                continue
            out.append({"id": it["id"], "date": p["datetime"][:10],
                        "vv": a["vv"]["href"], "vh": a["vh"]["href"]})
        nxt = [l for l in page.get("links", []) if l.get("rel") == "next"]
        if not nxt or not feats:
            break
        body = nxt[0].get("body") or body
        if "token" not in body:
            break
    out.sort(key=lambda r: (r["date"], r["id"]))
    return out

def block_grids():
    """A 76 by 76 window of 10 m Equi7 cells centred on each block, snapped to
    the grid, so every cell edge sits on a multiple of 10 m in EPSG:27705."""
    blocks = gpd.read_file(BLOCKS).to_crs(DST)
    grids = []
    for i, geom in enumerate(blocks.geometry):
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = geom.bounds
        cx, cy = (minx + maxx) / 2, (miny + maxy) / 2
        x0 = round(cx / RES) * RES - (NCELL // 2) * RES
        y1 = round(cy / RES) * RES + (NCELL // 2) * RES
        grids.append({"block": f"block_{i + 1:03d}", "x0": x0, "y1": y1,
                      "bounds": (x0, y1 - NCELL * RES, x0 + NCELL * RES, y1)})
    return grids

def read_one(src, g):
    """Read one block window and lay it on the 10 m Equi7 grid. The source
    window is clipped to the scene rather than read boundless, because a
    boundless read in rasterio is an order of magnitude slower over HTTP."""
    x0, ymin, x1, ymax = g["bounds"]
    sx0, sy0, sx1, sy1 = transform_bounds(DST, src.crs, x0, ymin, x1, ymax,
                                          densify_pts=21)
    pad = 2 * abs(src.transform.a)
    sw = from_bounds(sx0 - pad, sy0 - pad, sx1 + pad, sy1 + pad, src.transform)
    sw = sw.intersection(Window(0, 0, src.width, src.height)) \
        if (sw.col_off < src.width and sw.row_off < src.height and
            sw.col_off + sw.width > 0 and sw.row_off + sw.height > 0) else None
    dst = np.zeros((NCELL, NCELL), dtype="float32")
    if sw is None or sw.width < 1 or sw.height < 1:
        return dst
    sw = sw.round_offsets().round_lengths()
    arr_src = src.read(1, window=sw).astype("float32")
    reproject(source=arr_src, destination=dst,
              src_transform=src.window_transform(sw), src_crs=src.crs,
              dst_transform=from_origin(x0, ymax, RES, RES), dst_crs=DST,
              resampling=Resampling.average, src_nodata=0, dst_nodata=0)
    return dst

def one_scene(args):
    """One scene, every block, on one open handle per polarisation."""
    sc, grids = args
    for attempt in range(1, 5):
        try:
            tk = token()
            out = np.full((2, len(grids), NCELL, NCELL), np.nan, "float32")
            for bi, href in enumerate((sc["vv"], sc["vh"])):
                with rasterio.open(f"{href}?{tk}") as src:
                    for gi, g in enumerate(grids):
                        arr = read_one(src, g)
                        out[bi, gi] = np.where(arr > 0, arr, np.nan)
            final = CACHE / f"{sc['id']}.npy"
            with open(final.with_name(final.name + ".part"), "wb") as fh:
                np.save(fh, out)
            os.replace(final.with_name(final.name + ".part"), final)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            if "403" in str(e):
                with _lock:
                    _tok["e"] = 0.0
            if attempt < 4:
                time.sleep(15 * attempt)
                continue
            print(f"  skip {sc['id']} after {attempt} attempts: {type(e).__name__}", flush=True)
            return False

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--shard", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--nshards", type=int, default=1)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUTDIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    grids = block_grids()
    scenes = scenes_on_track()
    todo = [s for i, s in enumerate(scenes)
            if i % a.nshards == a.shard and not (CACHE / f"{s['id']}.npy").exists()]
    print(f"{len(scenes)} scenes on track {TRACK}, shard {a.shard} of {a.nshards} "
          f"reads {len(todo)}, {len(grids)} blocks of {NCELL} by {NCELL} at {RES} m "
          f"on EPSG:27705", flush=True)
    t0 = time.time()
    n_fail = 0
    for i, sc in enumerate(todo):
        n_fail += not one_scene((sc, grids))
        if (i + 1) % 5 == 0:
            print(f"  shard {a.shard}: {i + 1}/{len(todo)}, {n_fail} failed, "
                  f"{time.time() - t0:.0f}s", flush=True)
    print(f"shard {a.shard} read in {time.time() - t0:.0f}s, {n_fail} failed", flush=True)
    if a.nshards > 1:
        return

    # Reshuffle the per-scene cache into one memory-mapped array per block.
    have = [s for s in scenes if (CACHE / f"{s['id']}.npy").exists()]
    missing = [s["id"] for s in scenes if s not in have]
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{len(missing)} of {len(scenes)} scenes are not in the cache, "
                           f"so the block stacks would be incomplete; rerun the shards. "
                           f"First missing: {missing[:5]}")
    n = len(have)
    mm = [np.lib.format.open_memmap(OUTDIR / f"{g['block']}.npy", mode="w+",
                                    dtype="float32", shape=(n, 2, NCELL, NCELL))
          for g in grids]
    step = 40
    for k in range(0, n, step):
        chunk = np.stack([np.load(CACHE / f"{s['id']}.npy") for s in have[k:k + step]])
        for gi in range(len(grids)):
            mm[gi][k:k + chunk.shape[0]] = chunk[:, :, gi]
        print(f"  reshuffled {min(k + step, n)}/{n}", flush=True)
    for m in mm:
        m.flush()
    np.savez(OUTDIR / "meta.npz",
             scene_id=np.array([s["id"] for s in have]),
             date=np.array([s["date"] for s in have]),
             block=np.array([g["block"] for g in grids]),
             x0=np.array([g["x0"] for g in grids], "float64"),
             y1=np.array([g["y1"] for g in grids], "float64"),
             bands=np.array(["VV", "VH"]), res_m=RES, ncell=NCELL, track=TRACK,
             crs="EPSG:27705")
    print(f"wrote {len(grids)} block stacks of ({n}, 2, {NCELL}, {NCELL}) to "
          f"{OUTDIR.name}", flush=True)

if not (OUTDIR / "meta.npz").exists():
    import sys
    sys.argv = [sys.argv[0]]
    main()
```

```{python}
#| label: radar-cube
#| echo: true
#| output: false
#| python.reticulate: false
#| engine.path: /opt/local/bin/python3
import csv
import os
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import rasterio
# The R session this runs in sets PROJ_LIB to an R package's own PROJ database,
# which rasterio's PROJ cannot read, so point it at the system PROJ data.
import rasterio._env
try:
    import pyproj
    _proj = pyproj.datadir.get_data_dir()
except ImportError:
    _proj = next((d for d in ("/opt/local/lib/proj9/share/proj", "/opt/local/share/proj",
                              "/usr/local/share/proj", "/usr/share/proj")
                  if os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, "proj.db"))), None)
if _proj:
    os.environ["PROJ_LIB"] = os.environ["PROJ_DATA"] = _proj
    rasterio._env.set_proj_data_search_path(_proj)
import geopandas as gpd
from rasterio.transform import from_origin

ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "02.inputs").is_dir())
IN = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_blocks_10m"
FLT = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_blocks_10m_mtfiltered"
CUBE = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "s1_cube_10m"
BLOCKS = ROOT / "02.inputs" / "derived" / "sample_blocks.gpkg"
FLOOR = ROOT / "03.outputs" / "radar_noise_floor_undamaged_10m.csv"
MONTHS = (6, 7, 8, 9)
W = 3

def local_mean(a, w):
    r = w // 2
    valid = np.isfinite(a)
    filled = np.where(valid, a, 0.0)
    s = np.zeros_like(filled)
    n = np.zeros(filled.shape, dtype="int16")
    for dy in range(-r, r + 1):
        for dx in range(-r, r + 1):
            s += np.roll(np.roll(filled, dy, axis=-2), dx, axis=-1)
            n += np.roll(np.roll(valid, dy, axis=-2), dx, axis=-1)
    out = np.divide(s, np.maximum(n, 1), where=n > 0)
    out[..., :r, :] = np.nan
    out[..., -r:, :] = np.nan
    out[..., :, :r] = np.nan
    out[..., :, -r:] = np.nan
    out[n == 0] = np.nan
    return out

def mt_filter(stack):
    """stack (scene, band, row, col) for one block."""
    out = np.full_like(stack, np.nan)
    for bi in range(stack.shape[1]):
        I = stack[:, bi]
        E = np.stack([local_mean(I[k], W) for k in range(I.shape[0])])
        ok = np.isfinite(I) & np.isfinite(E) & (E != 0)
        ratio = np.where(ok, I / np.where(E == 0, np.nan, E), 0.0)
        c = ok.sum(axis=0)
        mean_ratio = np.where(c > 0, ratio.sum(axis=0) / np.maximum(c, 1), np.nan)
        out[:, bi] = np.where(ok, E * mean_ratio[None, ...], np.nan)
    return out

def db(a):
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        return 10 * np.log10(a)

def floors(x, dates):
    """x (scene, row, col) in dB for one band and block; returns (rep, yr)."""
    years = np.array([int(d[:4]) for d in dates])
    months = np.array([int(d[5:7]) for d in dates])
    rep, yr = [], []
    for m in MONTHS:
        monthly = {}
        for y in sorted(set(years)):
            sel = (years == y) & (months == m)
            if sel.sum() == 0:
                continue
            a = x[sel]
            n = np.isfinite(a).sum(axis=0)
            if sel.sum() >= 2:
                sd = np.nanstd(a, axis=0, ddof=1)
                rep.append(sd[n >= 2])
            monthly[y] = np.nanmean(a, axis=0)
        if len(monthly) >= 4:
            s = np.stack([monthly[y] for y in sorted(monthly)])
            n = np.isfinite(s).sum(axis=0)
            sd = np.nanstd(s, axis=0, ddof=1)
            yr.append(sd[n >= 4])
    rep = np.concatenate(rep) if rep else np.array([])
    yr = np.concatenate(yr) if yr else np.array([])
    return rep[np.isfinite(rep)], yr[np.isfinite(yr)]

def main():
    FLT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    CUBE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    z = np.load(IN / "meta.npz", allow_pickle=False)
    dates, blocks, x0s, y1s = z["date"], z["block"], z["x0"], z["y1"]
    res, ncell = int(z["res_m"]), int(z["ncell"])
    undamaged = ~gpd.read_file(BLOCKS)["damage"].astype(bool).to_numpy()
    first, last = str(dates[0])[:7], str(dates[-1])[:7]
    y0, m0 = int(first[:4]), int(first[5:])
    y1_, m1 = int(last[:4]), int(last[5:])
    months = [f"{y}-{m:02d}" for y in range(y0, y1_ + 1) for m in range(1, 13)
              if (y, m) >= (y0, m0) and (y, m) <= (y1_, m1)]
    by_month = defaultdict(list)
    for i, d in enumerate(dates):
        by_month[str(d)[:7]].append(i)
    print(f"{len(blocks)} blocks, {len(dates)} scenes, {len(months)} months "
          f"{first} to {last}", flush=True)
    acc = {("unfiltered", b): [[], []] for b in ("VV", "VH")}
    acc.update({("mt_filtered", b): [[], []] for b in ("VV", "VH")})
    for gi, blk in enumerate(blocks):
        tile = f"B{blk[-3:]}"
        raw = np.load(IN / f"{blk}.npy", mmap_mode="r")
        fpath = FLT / f"{blk}.npy"
        if fpath.exists():
            flt = np.load(fpath, mmap_mode="r")
        else:
            flt = mt_filter(np.asarray(raw))
            with open(fpath.with_name(fpath.name + ".part"), "wb") as fh:
                np.save(fh, flt)
            os.replace(fpath.with_name(fpath.name + ".part"), fpath)
        if undamaged[gi]:
            for label, st in (("unfiltered", raw), ("mt_filtered", flt)):
                for bi, band in enumerate(("VV", "VH")):
                    rep, yr = floors(db(np.asarray(st[:, bi])), dates)
                    acc[(label, band)][0].append(rep)
                    acc[(label, band)][1].append(yr)
        tr = from_origin(x0s[gi], y1s[gi], res, res)
        prof = dict(driver="GTiff", dtype="float32", count=1, nodata=np.nan,
                    width=ncell, height=ncell, crs="EPSG:27705", transform=tr,
                    compress="deflate", predictor=2)
        for m in months:
            idx = by_month.get(m, [])
            for bi, band in enumerate(("VV", "VH")):
                path = CUBE / f"SENTINEL-1_RTC_{tile}_{band}_{m}-01.tif"
                if path.exists():
                    continue
                with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
                    comp = (np.nanmean(flt[idx, bi], axis=0) if idx
                            else np.full((ncell, ncell), np.nan, "float32"))
                part = path.with_name(path.name + ".part")
                with rasterio.open(part, "w", **prof) as dst:
                    dst.write(comp.astype("float32"), 1)
                    dst.update_tags(scenes=len(idx), month=m, res_m=res,
                                    track=int(z["track"]), filter="quegan2000_3x3",
                                    units="gamma0 linear power")
                os.replace(part, path)
        if gi % 20 == 0:
            print(f"  {blk} done", flush=True)
    rows = []
    for (label, band), (rep, yr) in acc.items():
        rep, yr = np.concatenate(rep), np.concatenate(yr)
        rows.append({"processing": label, "band": band,
                     "repeatability_median_db": round(float(np.median(rep)), 3),
                     "repeatability_n": int(rep.size),
                     "year_to_year_median_db": round(float(np.median(yr)), 3),
                     "year_to_year_q25_db": round(float(np.percentile(yr, 25)), 3),
                     "year_to_year_q75_db": round(float(np.percentile(yr, 75)), 3),
                     "year_to_year_n": int(yr.size),
                     "blocks": int(undamaged.sum()), "months": "6-9",
                     "support": "10 m cell"})
    with FLOOR.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"wrote {FLOOR.name} and the cube under {CUBE.name}", flush=True)

if not FLOOR.exists():
    main()
```

```{python}
import os, csv
import numpy as np

if not os.path.exists("03.outputs/filter_effect_block.csv"):
    z = np.load("02.inputs/derived/s1_blocks_10m/meta.npz")
    dates, blocks, x0, y1 = z["date"], z["block"], z["x0"], z["y1"]
    di = next(i for i, d in enumerate(dates) if str(d).startswith("2019-07"))
    for k, b in enumerate(blocks):
        raw = np.load(f"02.inputs/derived/s1_blocks_10m/{b}.npy", mmap_mode="r")[di, 0]
        if np.isfinite(raw[1:-1, 1:-1]).all():
            break
    flt = np.load(f"02.inputs/derived/s1_blocks_10m_mtfiltered/{b}.npy", mmap_mode="r")[di, 0]
    with open("03.outputs/filter_effect_block.csv", "w", newline="") as fh:
        w = csv.writer(fh)
        w.writerow(["block", "date", "x0", "y1", "before", "after"])
        w.writerows([b, dates[di], x0[k], y1[k], r, a] for r, a in
                    zip(np.asarray(raw).ravel(), np.asarray(flt).ravel()))
```

```{r}
#| label: filter-effect
#| echo: true
#| output: false
fe <- read.csv("03.outputs/filter_effect_block.csv")
n <- sqrt(nrow(fe))
fe_r <- rast(nrows = n, ncols = n, xmin = fe$x0[1], xmax = fe$x0[1] + 10 * n,
             ymin = fe$y1[1] - 10 * n, ymax = fe$y1[1], crs = "EPSG:27705",
             nlyrs = 2, names = c("before", "after"))
values(fe_r) <- 10 * log10(as.matrix(fe[, c("before", "after")]))
fe_lim <- range(values(fe_r), na.rm = TRUE)
fe_sd <- apply(values(fe_r), 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE)
filter_cap <- paste0(
  "One block on one date before and after the multi-temporal speckle filter, ",
  "VV backscatter in decibels at ", res(fe_r)[1], " m over the ", n, " by ", n,
  " cells of the window of block ", as.integer(sub("block_", "", fe$block[1])), " on ",
  format(as.Date(fe$date[1]), "%d %B %Y"), ", on one colour range. The filter ",
  "takes each date's ratio to its own local mean in a 3 by 3 window and ",
  "averages those ratios across every date in the series, so the outer ring ",
  "of cells, where the window has no neighbour, is left empty. The standard ",
  "deviation across the block's cells fell from ", sprintf("%.2f", fe_sd[["before"]]),
  " to ", sprintf("%.2f", fe_sd[["after"]]), " dB. WGS 84 Equi7 North America ",
  "(EPSG:27705), graticule in m."
)
```

```{r}
fe_panel <- function(lyr, title, legend) {
  tm_shape(fe_r[[lyr]]) +
    tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = "viridis", limits = fe_lim),
              col.legend = legend) +
    map_frame(title, legend = tm_pos_in("right", "bottom"), n.x = 3, n.y = 3)
}
tmap_arrange(
  fe_panel("before", "(a) Before the filter", tm_legend_hide()),
  fe_panel("after", "(b) After the filter",
           tm_legend(title = "VV (dB)", reverse = TRUE, height = 6)),
  ncol = 2, outer.margins = 0.01
)
```

The chain was checked against the Sentinel-1 Global Backscatter Model [@Bauer_Marschallinger_2021], an independent processor's mean of 2016 and 2017, which across the `r s1val$n_blocks[1]` blocks agreed in pattern at a correlation of `r sprintf("%.3f", s1val$pearson_r[s1val$band == "VV"])` in VV and `r sprintf("%.3f", s1val$pearson_r[s1val$band == "VH"])` in VH, with level offsets of `r sprintf("%.2f", s1val$offset_db[s1val$band == "VV"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", s1val$offset_db[s1val$band == "VH"])` dB decomposed in the supplement. The noise floor, the year-to-year spread of one cell's mean for the same calendar month on the `r unique(s1_floor30$blocks)` blocks the aerial survey never recorded damage in, June through September after the filter, was `r sprintf("%.2f", yr_floor("VV"))` dB in VV and `r sprintf("%.2f", yr_floor("VH"))` dB in VH, against total canopy removal by windthrow of `r sprintf("%.2f", ref_db("windthrow_vv_db"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", ref_db("windthrow_vh_db"))` dB [@R_etschi_2019, page 11], ratios of `r sprintf("%.2f", canopy_ratio[["VV"]])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", canopy_ratio[["VH"]])`, so at one cell in one year total canopy removal sat at the floor; the model reads a trajectory across months and years rather than one difference, and its floor is what the pre-registered tests measure. The filtered stack was composited to calendar month and written as a local cube for the sits package, `r format(length(s1_cube_files), big.mark = ",")` rasters over `r length(s1_cube_dates)` months from `r format(min(s1_cube_dates), "%B %Y")` to `r format(max(s1_cube_dates), "%B %Y")`, from which the models receive the Kennaugh elements K0 and K1, the sum and the difference of the VV and VH intensities after @Hechtl_2025, in decibels; @fig-season draws the cube's July and November of one year block by block.

```{r}
#| label: season-data
#| echo: true
#| output: false
k0_blocks <- function(month) {
  sapply(seq_len(nrow(blocks)), function(i) {
    r <- rast(sprintf("02.inputs/derived/s1_cube_10m/SENTINEL-1_RTC_B%03d_%s_2020-%02d-01.tif",
                      i, c("VV", "VH"), month))
    10 * log10(sum(global(mask(r, vect(st_transform(blocks[i, ], "EPSG:27705"))), "mean", na.rm = TRUE)$mean))
  })
}
blocks$k0_jul <- k0_blocks(7)
blocks$k0_nov <- k0_blocks(11)
k0_lim <- range(c(blocks$k0_jul, blocks$k0_nov), na.rm = TRUE)
season_cap <- paste0(
  "K0, the sum of the VV and VH intensities in decibels, per sampled block from ",
  "the filtered monthly cube, (a) July and (b) November 2020, on one colour ",
  "range from ", sprintf("%.1f", k0_lim[1]), " to ", sprintf("%.1f", k0_lim[2]),
  " dB. Each square is the mean of the 10 m cells inside one block, drawn ",
  "larger than the block. Across the ",
  sum(complete.cases(blocks$k0_jul, blocks$k0_nov)), " blocks holding both ",
  "months, July sat ", sprintf("%.2f", mean(blocks$k0_jul - blocks$k0_nov,
                                             na.rm = TRUE)),
  " dB above November. The dashed orange rectangle is the confirmatory study ",
  "window. WGS 84 UTM zone 5N (EPSG:32605), graticule in km."
)
```
